target.title: fix(agents): keep background exec exit notifications UTF-16 safe at the snippet cut
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who enable background exec exit notifications (`notifyOnExit`) can receive a broken/replacement character in their chat channel. When completed background command output is trimmed for the `Exec completed/failed (...) :: <output>` notification, either the 400-character tail source or the final 180-character snippet could previously split an emoji's UTF-16 surrogate pair.

While addressing review, this also applies the same suffix-cut rule to the sibling node-host exec approval follow-up summary, which uses the same user-visible output tail pattern after an approved remote node run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The notification path now keeps both truncation points UTF-16 safe: the shared `tail()` helper uses `sliceUtf16Safe` for suffix cuts, and the notification snippet compactor uses `truncateUtf16Safe` before appending the ellipsis. The node-host approval follow-up suffix cut now also uses `sliceUtf16Safe` instead of a raw negative `slice`. ASCII/BMP output and the existing ellipsis behavior are unchanged. Risk is limited to exec output retention/notification strings; this does not change process execution, routing, permissions, or channel transport behavior.

## User Impact

Background exec completion notifications and node-host exec approval follow-up summaries no longer show a broken character when emoji output lands at their truncation boundaries. Ordinary output remains unchanged, and long snippets are still compacted with `…` where that path already used an ellipsis.

## Evidence

`maybeNotifyOnExit` in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts` takes `tail(..., DEFAULT_NOTIFY_TAIL_CHARS)` and then compacts that text before calling `enqueueSystemEvent`, so the original defect is in the runtime notification string before any channel transport sees it. The node-host approval follow-up in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.ts` similarly formats a user-visible output tail before sending the follow-up result.

Focused regressions now cover:

- final snippet cut: emoji high surrogate at the 180-character compaction edge
- notify tail source: output longer than 400 characters where the 400-character tail would start inside an emoji
- node-host approval follow-up: approved remote node output where the follow-up tail would start inside an emoji

Real runtime proof for the background notification path after this fix, using the actual `runExecProcess` path and real system-event queue (`runExecProcess` -> backgrounded exit -> `enqueueSystemEvent` -> `drainSystemEvents`):

```json
{
  "outcome": "completed",
  "eventCount": 1,
  "notification": "Exec completed (tidal-nu, code 0) :: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb…",
  "hasLoneSurrogate": false,
  "hasReplacementCharacter": false,
  "includesTailHead": true
}
```

Commands run:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts src/shared/utf16-slice.test.ts` -> pass
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/bash-process-registry.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts` -> pass
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/bash-process-registry.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts` -> pass
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo` -> pass
- `node --import tsx --input-type=module ...` real runtime proof above -> pass

What was not tested: no live Telegram/Discord channel round-trip was exercised. The failure and fix are before transport, in the exact user-visible text handed to delivery/follow-up, so the real runtime proof plus focused node-host follow-up regression cover the affected boundaries; full broad validation runs in CI.

AI-assisted: implemented and validated with AI assistance; the commands and outputs above were run for real.
